newsitem.title: USA: Cooper sees fiscal 1996 net above target.
newsitem.headline: Cooper sees fiscal 1996 net above target.

text.p: Cooper Cos Inc said it expects to exceed the upper range of its previously announced earnings target of $1.30 to $1.35 per share for the year ending October 31, including a deferred tax benefit of over $0.30 per share.

In 1995, Cooper reported earnings of $0.01 per share with no deferred tax benefit. It also said it initially estimates fiscal 1997 earnings per share in the range of $1.55 to $1.65 including a deferred tax benefit of about $0.15 per share. Revenue and operating income for 1997 are expected to grow by more than 15 percent and 30 percent, respectively.

"In 1996, we will deliver the double-digit revenue growth we have been forecasting throughout the year. Revenue will top the $108 million mark and grow more than 11 percent overall," said Thomas Bender, chief executive officer.
The company said its CooperVision contact lens business and CooperSurgical gynecology device business will report strong revenue and operating income growth.
Bender said consolidated fourth quarter revenue is expected to grow more than 20 percent, with consolidated quarterly operating income more than doubling.
"During each quarter of 1996, the percentage gain year to year was greater than the previous quarter's comparison."
